topic: Pringles inventor Fredric Baur asked for his ashes to be buried in a Pringles can
title: The Pringles Inventor Was Buried in a Pringles Can
note: Gemini first draft, NOT fact-checked. Claude must verify every claim with its own 2-source rule before using any of it in a real job file.
draft_script: You know Pringles. That iconic stackable chip. But do you know the man behind it? His name was Fredric Baur. Baur was a food technician. He also was a chemist. He designed the Pringles chip itself. He created the unique saddle shape. This allowed the chips to stack. He also invented the famous cylindrical can. This kept the chips from breaking. It was a packaging breakthrough. Baur's work changed snack food. He secured seven patents for Pringles. He was proud of his invention. But his story has a strange ending. In 2008, Baur died. He was 89 years old. His family fulfilled a final request. He wanted his remains buried in a Pringles can. Not just any can. An original Pringles can. His ashes were placed inside. He is now buried in a Pringles can. It's a bizarre final tribute. A true business legacy. Even in death. A product's inventor, forever linked to his creation.
